A 51-year-old homeless man is brought to the emergency department after being found unresponsive
with multiple empty pill bottles nearby. His history includes recurrent pancreatitis, dehydration, suicide
attempts, and IV drug use. His vital signs show: temperature 98.2°F (37.3°C), blood pressure 106/52
mmHg, pulse 136/min, respirations 29/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. He has a Glasgow
coma scale of 6. Laboratory results show: Hematology: - Hemoglobin: 10 g/dL - Hematocrit: 30% -
Leukocyte count: 5,500/mm^3 (normal differential) - Platelet count: 147,000/mm^3 Serum Studies: -
Albumin: 1.9 g/dL - Na+: 139 mEq/L - Cl-: 100 mEq/L - K+: 4.3 mEq/L - HCO3-: 25 mEq/L - BUN: 29
mg/dL - Glucose: 65 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.5 mg/dL - Ca2+: 7.2 mg/dL - Prothrombin time: 27 seconds -
Partial thromboplastin time: 67 seconds - AST: 12 U/L - ALT: 10 U/L What is the most effective
treatment for the underlying pathology? Answer Choices: (A) Intravenous dextrose infusion (B)
Supportive therapy, thiamine, dextrose, naloxone, and NPO (C) Liver transplant (D) Hemodialysis (E)
Parenteral vitamin K administration (F) Fresh frozen plasma transfusion (G) High-dose corticosteroid
therapy (H) Colloid-containing fluids (I) Chelation therapy for heavy metal toxicity (J) Administration of
N-acetylcysteine
